# `upload_refstar_info`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Store a list of reference stars on the device for later use.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xe2f40, CheckDirConst @0x6ece40, WriteFile @0x6df730, reader StackFunc @0x19c3c0 with LoadPmRef @0x203460 (64-bit build); error sites: 257 at CheckDirConst @0x6ed018; 258 at WriteFile @0x6df71c; 218 at @0x6df640, @0x6df69c, @0x6df6d8 |

Serialises the supplied refData array unchanged and writes it as the reference-star file (ref_stars.json) in the device's AI-processing temporary directory, creating the directory when needed. The device does not interpret the stars here. The file is read by the imager's own stacking worker; in the photometry stacking mode (capture type 2) it loads the file as the reference-star list. READ; that capture type 2 is the photometry/check stack mode is INFERRED. Synchronous writes without timeout. Firmware 9.75, app 3.4.0 writes ref_stars.json through a temporary file (name suffixed with the process id) and renames it; a rename failure removes the temporary file and gives 515. The handler gives 107 and 102 itself; 257, 258 and 218 still come from the directory-check and file-write helpers. READ (64-bit build). The 32-bit build has the temporary-file string; its codes are INFERRED the same.

Side effects: Creates the target directory if missing and writes (replaces) the reference-star file.

| `params.refData` | array<any> | no | - | Reference-star records. Elements are not parsed or validated; the whole array is serialised unchanged to the device's reference-star file. Empty array allowed; no size bound. The app sends NearbyStarData records (app-side shape INFERRED, not enforced by the device). [READ] |
| `params.refData:` | array<any> | no | - | Fallback alias key, literally including the trailing colon, read only when refData is absent. A wrong-typed refData does not fall back. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 107 | params absent, null, positional array, or otherwise not an object | `expected object param` |
| 102 | Neither refData nor the alias key present, or refData is not an array | `invalid params` |
| 515 | Firmware 9.75: renaming the temporary file to ref_stars.json failed | `rename ref star file fail` |
| 257 | The reference-star directory could not be created | `create directory failed` |
| 258 | The file could not be opened for writing | `open file failed` |
| 218 | A short write, or a flush or sync failure | `fail to write file` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

(Firmware 9.31 behaviour; 9.75 adds 515.) Failures of the directory check and of the file write return their error code as the method's error (257 from the directory check; 258 and 218 from the file write). The helper's 209 for an empty directory name is unreachable because the directory is a constant (INFERRED). No result member on handler errors.

## Example

Request, empty - Empty list:

```json
{"id":66,"method":"upload_refstar_info","params":{"refData":[]}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"upload_refstar_info","result":0,"code":0,"id":66}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"upload_refstar_info","error":"invalid params","code":102,"id":67}
```
